svg.text: The Anti-hero's glasses: scary shiny glasses

Orb: the rival is our resident scary shiny glasses character. Six frames in his blade and plate language; the best two in three lens states (clear, glare, glint); where the glare fires; and what battle damage
does. Unmasked faces (the masks stay parked). Working labels, pending Legal review.
1. Six frames to Legal's rules; frame C is Orb's pick (clear and glare; at 72, 24 and 12 px; and in profile at fight size)
Dropped for Legal (RL-066): thin round wire lenses, narrow tinted rectangles (my slits), a half-rim with a brow bar, and the single bar across both eyes (a visor). Lenses are never a display: no
readout, scan bar or overlay, and the earlier scan-like streaks are gone.
1 Blade lenses, chamfers dropped
approved by Orb
profile, clear and glare
72 and 24 px
12 px eye band: clear, glare (and in grey)
APPROVED by Orb (2026-10-04): a bare four-sided
wedge with a thin even rim, no lit line, no tabs.
The plainest; almost ordinary until the glare, and
then one pale wedge on a fully opaque lens.
2 Blade lenses
profile, clear and glare
72 and 24 px
12 px eye band: clear, glare (and in grey)
Blade lenses with the lit plate line along the top
edge: Art's earlier pick, the runner-up. Tapered
wedge lenses, tips level, never upswept.
3 Cut hex
profile, clear and glare
72 and 24 px
12 px eye band: clear, glare (and in grey)
A hexagonal lens cut asymmetrically (one corner
chopped long, the outer corner a point): his
hexagon in its smallest, most ordinary form.
4 Shard
profile, clear and glare
72 and 24 px
12 px eye band: clear, glare (and in grey)
A tapered shard, wide at the nose and pointed at
the temple: the coldest silhouette; reads almost
as a slash of tint at 12 px.
5 Slash cut
profile, clear and glare
72 and 24 px
12 px eye band: clear, glare (and in grey)
A five-sided slash cut, no two sides parallel: the
most unusual, and the one least like any ordinary
glasses.
6 Kite
profile, clear and glare
72 and 24 px
12 px eye band: clear, glare (and in grey)
A kite with the high point toward the nose: a
different rhythm to the others; the glare wedge
sits well in it.
2. The best two: clear, glare, glint (the glint sweeps left to right across both lenses in about 0.5 s; three moments are shown)
Blade lenses, chamfers dropped (frame C: approved by Orb)
clear: a dark violet tint, eyes dimly
visible
glare: the lens opaque, one hard-edged pale
wedge, eyes hidden; the smirk carries the
face (0.4 s at most)
glint: one moving wedge on the clear lens,
eyes dimly visible
the glint sweep: start, middle, end
profile at fight size: clear, then glare
Frame C, approved by Orb: the bare wedge. The lens is a dark violet
tint with the eyes dimly visible; in the glare the lens goes fully
opaque and the eyes are hidden completely, with one hard-edged
pale-violet wedge across it. The rim is thin and even, so the glasses
are nearly ordinary until the glare.
Blade lenses (the runner-up)
clear: a dark violet tint, eyes dimly
visible
glare: the lens opaque, one hard-edged pale
wedge, eyes hidden; the smirk carries the
face (0.4 s at most)
glint: one moving wedge on the clear lens,
eyes dimly visible
the glint sweep: start, middle, end
profile at fight size: clear, then glare
The runner-up: the same wedge with the lit plate line along the top
edge (Art's earlier pick), kept for comparison.
His gesture (Legal: a nudge at the temple arm, or with the back of the forearm plate; never one finger at the bridge, never folded or steepled hands before the face)
a nudge at the temple arm (glare)
the back of the forearm plate (glare)
The glare fires on the nudge: the hand or forearm comes up to the temple, the lens flashes for 0.4 s, and the arm drops.
The same gesture without the glare is his idle tell when Pride is rising. It is never done with a finger at the bridge,
and the hands are never folded or steepled in front of the face or mouth. Lines said with it come from Narrative's bank
in his own voice: none of the stock lines that go with the trope.
3. Where the glare fires (for Game Design and VFX)
The staredown (the round intro, the camera push-in)
a single glint sweeps across the lenses once, eyes dimly visible: he is watching you.
His taunt
the glare for 0.4 s with the smirk as the only face, then it clears.
Entering On the Chin
the glare on the entry beat (he reads the blow), 0.4 s, then it clears.
A signature or a finisher
a glint at the very start of the wind-up only; never a glare during the charge, a rubble ring or lightning (that would stack marks).
Pride thresholds
each threshold crossed gives a glint, then a one-lens flash, then a full glare at the top: more Pride, more glare. Each is 0.4 s at most.
The seal break (the Proud front breaks)
the lens cracks (stage 2 below) and the glare falters. Never at a transformation break, and never with a shouted form name.

Rules for VFX (RL-066): a quick attack and a hold of 0.4 s at most, then clear; key moments only (reading a move, pride, a taunt, the seal break), never every exchange; at most one glare in any 3 s. The glare is one hard-edged

wedge in a pale violet, never white, gold, orange or red, never a round disc with a star. One slow fade in and out, no strobing (photosensitivity); with reduced motion it is a held tint with no sweep.

4. What battle damage does to them (the lead above, the second below): fresh, stage 1 scuffed, stage 2 torn, stage 3 ruined, each in clear and in glare; and glasses knocked off by a hit (both allowed)
fresh
stage 1: scuffed
stage 2: torn
stage 3: ruined
knocked off by a hit
fresh
stage 1: scuffed
stage 2: torn
stage 3: ruined
knocked off by a hit

Stage 1: a hairline scratch across one lens and a nick on the rim; the glare still works. Stage 2: a single crack runs across the far lens and the far half of the frame bends and tilts; the glare gets a dark line in it. Stage 3:

the near lens cracks twice, a shard is gone from the corner of the far lens (the eye stays covered), the frame is bent and dropped, the bridge twists. Cracks never cross, and the glare falters: it is the first thing a beaten Pride
loses. A cracked lens and glasses knocked off by a hit are both fine under the rules and count as no mark.
For Legal, and for Orb

Legal (RL-066), how each rule is met: angular, tapered and hexagonal lenses cut asymmetrically in a thin violet frame (none round, none a narrow rectangle, no half-rim, no visor bar); normal lenses a dark violet tint; no goatee or

beard; no readout, scan bar or overlay on any lens; the glare is one hard-edged wedge in a pale violet (not white, never gold, orange or red) with no disc and no star, held 0.4 s at most, at key moments only, never at a

transformation break; the gesture is a nudge at the temple arm or the back of the forearm, never one finger at the bridge and never folded hands. Legal looks at the six frames, the glare wedge and the gesture sketch.

Decided by Orb (2026-10-04): frame C, and the glare hides his eyes completely. Still open: are the glasses always on, or do they appear for the taunt and the seal break only? The face stays recognisably him: the tail, the lit
slash, the sharp eyes.
